models.title: Future · which one? (reminder: present continuous, going to, will)

block.label: REMINDER · THREE FUTURES, WHICH ONE?
block.html:
PRESENT CONTINUOUS = an arrangement: it's in the calendar, with a day and time, and someone else knows.
I am meeting Ana at 6. · She is flying to Recife on Friday.

GOING TO = a plan I made before, or a prediction with evidence (I can see it).
I am going to start a course next year. · Look at those clouds! It is going to rain.

WILL = I decide now, I promise, I offer, or I think / believe.
The phone is ringing. I will get it! · I will call you tomorrow, I promise. · I think it will be a great year.

💡 Quick test: Is it in my calendar? → present continuous. Did I decide before? → going to. Did I decide right now? → will.

models.title: Relative clauses · what are they? (two sentences become one)

block.label: NEW · RELATIVE CLAUSES
block.html:
A relative clause gives information about a noun. It turns two sentences into one.

I have a friend. She lives in Lisbon.
→ I have a friend who lives in Lisbon.

This is the phone. I bought it yesterday.
→ This is the phone that I bought yesterday.

That's the restaurant. We had dinner there.
→ That's the restaurant where we had dinner.

💡 In Portuguese we use que for almost everything. In English, you choose the word by what you are talking about: a person, a thing, a place…

models.title: Relative pronouns · who, which, that, where, whose, when

block.label: THE RELATIVE PRONOUNS
rows: The woman who called you is my boss.
The car which I bought is red.
The car that I bought is red.
This is the city where I was born.
I have a friend whose father is a pilot.
I remember the day when we met.

models.title: Relative clauses · when can we omit the pronoun?

block.label: WHEN CAN WE OMIT IT?
block.html:
Look at the word right after who / which / that.

A VERB comes next → the pronoun is the subject → you can't omit it.
The woman who lives next door is a doctor.
I have a dog that loves the beach.
✗ The woman lives next door is a doctor.

A PERSON (I, you, she, my mom…) comes next → the pronoun is the object → you can omit it.
The book (that) I read was great.
The man (who) you met is my uncle.

⚠️ whose is never omitted. where is not omitted either.

⚠️ Don't repeat the object (it happens in Portuguese: "o livro que eu li ele"):
✗ The book that I read it was great. ✓ The book that I read was great.

⚠️ where needs a full sentence after it: ✗ the city where I visited ✓ the city (that) I visited ✓ the city where I lived
